newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Flooding remains in Australian cotton belt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Flooding remains in Australian cotton belt.

text.p: Flooding in Australia's main cotton belt had not fundamentally changed since yesterday but more water was on the way, Matthew Berry, grower services manager lower Namoi valley for Namoi Cotton Co-operative said on Tuesday.

The height of floodwaters had fallen slightly, but more floodwater was headed for the Namoi valley from neighbouring areas around Tamworth and Quirindi, he told Reuters from the northern New South Wales town of Wee Waa.
"Probably the worst is over," he said.
The height of the Namoi River reached seven metres at its peak on Monday while floodwaters rose to within 1.5 metres of the top of the seven metre levee bank, he said.
Floodwater from Tamworth and Quirindi now on the way to the Wee Waa cotton-growing area followed significant rain on neighbouring areas after the weekend downpour at Wee Waa.

Berry said the consensus in Wee Waa, in the centre of Australia's A$1.0 billion cotton industry, was that the current 1996/97 crop was likely to emerge at about 2.4 million 500-pound bales, less than the official forecast of 2.5 million bales.
Yields would be the main problem, although the cotton district was presently experiencing hot and sunny weather, he said.
Tropical cyclone Harold, off the north Queensland coast, was causing some concern in the cotton district, he said.
